_meta.indication: SIVEXTRO is an oxazolidinone-class antibacterial drug indicated in adults for the treatment of acute bacterial skin and skin structure infections (ABSSSI) caused by designated susceptible bacteria

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, multicenter noninferiority trial; oral tedizolid 200 mg daily for 6 days vs oral linezolid 600 mg every 12 hours for 10 days
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with acute bacterial skin and skin structure infections (ABSSSI) including cellulitis/erysipelas, major cutaneous abscess, and wound infections
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Early clinical response at 48-72 hours: no increase from baseline lesion area and oral temperature ≤ 37.6°C confirmed by a second measurement within 24 hours (ITT)
pivotal_trials.result: Early clinical response 256/323 (79.3%) tedizolid vs 258/326 (79.1%) linezolid; treatment difference 0.1 (95% CI -6.2, 6.3), meeting the -10% noninferiority margin

nct_ctgov.title: TR-701 FA vs. Linezolid for the Treatment of Acute Bacterial Skin and Skin Structure Infections.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, multicenter noninferiority trial; IV with switch to oral tedizolid 200 mg daily for 6 days vs IV/oral linezolid 600 mg every 12 hours for 10 days
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with ABSSSI (cellulitis/erysipelas, major cutaneous abscess, wound infection) who could receive oral therapy after a minimum of one day of IV therapy
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Early clinical response at 48-72 hours: at least a 20% decrease from baseline lesion area (ITT)
pivotal_trials.result: Early clinical response (≥20% lesion area decrease, Trial 2 primary endpoint) 283/332 (85.2%) tedizolid vs 276/334 (82.6%) linezolid; treatment difference 2.6 (95% CI -3.0, 8.2), with the CI lower bound above the -10% noninferiority margin

nct_ctgov.title: TR-701 FA vs Linezolid for the Treatment of Acute Bacterial Skin and Skin Structure Infections

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions were nausea (8%), headache (6%), diarrhea (4%), vomiting (3%), and dizziness (2%). Serious adverse reactions occurred in 1.8% and discontinuations due to adverse reactions in 0.5% of SIVEXTRO patients
target_moa: Tedizolid phosphate is a prodrug converted to tedizolid, which binds to the 50S subunit of the bacterial ribosome, inhibiting bacterial protein synthesis

advisory_committee.vote: Anti-Infective Drugs Advisory Committee (AIDAC) convened March 31, 2014; all committee members voted 'yes' that substantial evidence of safety and effectiveness was provided

basis.text: Granted QIDP designation under the GAIN Act of FDASIA 2012; qualifies for an additional five years of marketing exclusivity

citations.quote: Under the provisions of the Generating Antibiotic Incentives Now Act of the Food and Drug Administration Safety and Innovation Act of 2012, tedizolid tablets and powder for injection were granted Qualified Infectious Disease Product designation and therefore this application was granted a priority review. QIDP designation qualifies tedizolid for an additional five years of marketing exclusivity.

summary.text: Tedizolid phosphate (Sivextro), the second oxazolidinone-class antibacterial, received QIDP designation under the GAIN Act, which granted the application a priority review and an additional five years of marketing exclusivity. Approval for ABSSSI was based on two Phase 3 noninferiority trials versus linezolid, with the Anti-Infective Drugs Advisory Committee voting unanimously 'yes' on the evidence of safety and effectiveness.

Tedizolid phosphate is the second member in the class of antibacterial drugs known as oxazolidinones.
